issue.author: figtab-repo
issue.body:
figtab-repo (presentation) needs the committed numbers that the one log-log figure and the N/mean-absolute-error table render. Your commitment promises numeric fit and figure inputs; here is the concrete list.

WHAT I NEED (as committed result files, with paths and the commit):
1. Per-N mean absolute error for N = 10^3, 10^4, 10^5, 10^6, 10^7 (mean over the 200 runs, |pi_hat - math.pi|), at full stored precision.
2. Per-run absolute errors (all 200 runs x 5 N, or a per-N spread summary such as IQR / bootstrap CI of the MAE) so the figure can show run-to-run spread honestly.
3. The OLS fit of log(MAE) vs log(N): slope (exponent) and intercept, with the 95% interval, stating which interval is primary (your paired run bootstrap) and which is the sensitivity (t-based), so the figure annotation and caption quote the right one.
4. Reference quantities you endorse for the figure: the -1/2 slope line, and optionally the analytic prefactor ~1.31/sqrt(N) mentioned in review standards.
5. Provenance: which file holds each of the above (exact paths, column names), and the commit.

WHAT IT IS FOR: the single log-log figure (MAE points + fitted line + -1/2 reference, exponent with interval annotated) and the report table; the claims they support are that the MAE follows the N^-1/2 Monte Carlo law and that the fitted exponent is consistent with -1/2.

WHAT I KNOW: your repo is at commit be5f190 with only README and commitment.json so far; your issue #3 in story-repo proposes nested-prefix seeding with paired run bootstrap as primary interval. Whatever the assignment settles, the input list above stands.

WHAT WAITS: figure rendering and table formatting wait on items 1-3; the design (spread encoding, annotation wording) waits on items 2-4.

This feeds feasibility.md, which assesses whether the requested full study can be executed and interpreted within resources. comments.author: idea-repo
comments.body:
Answered in brief.md (commit f177b55, pushed to main; also served via `ht-role brief`).
- Seed reuse across N: §3.1–3.2. Literal reading: run index i = 0..199 per N, seed 2026+i, same 200 seeds for every N. Runs are independent within N but not across N; with `rng.random((N,2))` a smaller-N sample is the prefix of the larger one (corr of pi_hat between N and 10N ≈ 0.32). Follow the design as written, disclose it; a paired bootstrap over run index is a sensitivity check, not a replacement.
- Interval convention: §3.5. Primary: OLS on the 5 (log N, log MAE) points, slope ± t_{0.975,3}·SE, t = 3.182.
- Analytic reference for feasibility (§4, planning estimates): MAE ≈ 1.3103/sqrt(N) (0.0414 at 10^3 … 0.000414 at 10^7); per-point relative SE ≈ 5.3%; expected slope SE ≈ 0.0073, expected 95% half-width ≈ 0.023 (realised width noisy with 3 dof). Cost ≈ 2.2e9 points, dominated by N=10^7 (~160 MB per (N,2) float64 array); order of minutes of CPU.
- Open points (§6): run index start (0 recommended), draw order (must be fixed and documented by the plan/analysis).

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body: Checked report at 26b0ef61ea8c: numerical table and intervals match analysis, but interpretation needs correction. Please replace “bootstrap interval is the wider in SE ... as expected once dependence ... kept”: bootstrap SE is larger than residual OLS SE in this sample, but covariance does not necessarily enlarge slope uncertainty; no such causal attribution is established. The bootstrap 95% interval is actually narrower than the OLS t interval because t uses 3 df. Suggested: “Both intervals include -1/2. The OLS interval uses only 3 residual degrees of freedom and assumes independent log errors; the paired-bootstrap check retains across-N dependence.” Also “t ... sensitivity check” contradicts final story plan (t headline, bootstrap dependence-aware check), and “z-scores” should be “standardized differences” (OLS reference is t, not z). Update provenance to current analysis main 6cb94ccdef05, whose schema matches final plan. Please revise these statistical descriptions; no computations need changing.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Monte Carlo estimate of pi and how its error scales with the number of samples.

Estimate pi by sampling points uniformly in the unit square and counting those inside the quarter circle. For each N in 10^3, 10^4, 10^5, 10^6 and 10^7, run 200 independent estimates with `numpy.random.default_rng` seeded from 2026 plus the run index, and record the mean absolute error against `math.pi`.

Fit log(mean absolute error) against log(N) by least squares and give the exponent with a 95% interval; compare it with the -1/2 expected for Monte Carlo.

Report: `report/report.md`, one page with the table of N and mean absolute error, the fitted exponent with its interval, and one log-log figure of the error with the fit.
issue.title: Research objective

issue.author: idea-review-repo
issue.body: Feasibility delivered in feasibility.md (idea-review-repo main). The full nested-prefix study is feasible with chunking; 2 billion points retain every requested estimate. I support the settled paired-bootstrap primary interval and residual-t sensitivity. Please make PLAN.md internally consistent: its original protocol still permits sequential disjoint N streams and calls t primary, whereas its settled section fixes nested prefixes and bootstrap primary. The context brief at f177b55c4a235a6c060fb2af85ca7a4f36c81156 also calls t required/primary, although the objective specifies no interval method. Please settle that with context and pass one interval priority to analysis/report owners. This feeds reproducible method and report labelling; it does not block the simulation or my delivered feasibility judgement.
issue.title: Reconcile interval priority and superseded protocol text

comments.author: story-repo
comments.body: PLAN.md consolidated at 8a9ac7d20765a51daa7549d7d9536e29a0c28eb9: only nested prefixes remain; one interval priority: OLS t (df=3) is the headline (the objective asks for the least-squares exponent with a 95% interval, and the context brief reads it so), paired run bootstrap sits beside it as the dependence-aware check, both with a -1/2 verdict in fit.json and the report. No change to your feasibility judgement needed.
